subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm thinking a static vehicle model probably doesn't need joints at all, so I can keep it simple using the part, extrude, lathe, and rotation helpers without bothering with a skeleton.

Now I'm sketching out an armored APC-style truck: roughly 5.6m long, 2.4m wide, 2.6m tall with a turret, six wheels (three per side) sitting flush at y=0. I'm planning the chassis as a simple box, then building the sloped hull body by extruding a side profile (rear, roof, windshield, hood) along the width axis so it reads as an armored silhouette, and setting up the wheels as rotated cylinders.

Now I'm positioning the wheels along the body, adding neon hub rings and dark tires, and sketching simple fender/arch covers above them to hide the wheel-body overlap, then thinking through how to add a sloped, tinted windshield plane.

For the windshield, I'm computing the slope's normal vector and placing a plane angled to match the body's slope, with a cyan HUD-style glow texture, lifting it slightly to avoid clipping into the body geometry before moving on to the side windows.

Then I'm adding dark tinted side windows at x=±1.16 with glowing cyan edge textures, followed by a front bumper assembly with a steel push bar painted in yellow-black hazard stripes, magenta-white glowing headlights, and a textured grille plane, before starting on a roof-mounted neon light bar.

Next I'm detailing the vehicle's lighting and armament: alternating red/blue glow segments in the roof bar, magenta/cyan neon strips along the sides and underglow beneath the chassis, then building a roof-rear water cannon turret with a lathed base, rotating turret box, a forward-pointing barrel with a flared glowing nozzle, plus a horizontal water tank cylinder mounted at the back with a blue glow finish.

Setting barrel height at roughly 2.75 with total vehicle height near 2.95 feels right. I'm also thinking about adding details like armored side panels with hazard stripes and a fictional corporate decal — something like "NOVACORP RIOT UNIT" lettering on the door panel for flavor.

Now I'm working out exact placements: door panels sized 1.6x0.6 positioned symmetrically on each side, windows and logo text fitted into the remaining space without overlap, and figuring out which direction the decal text should face so it reads correctly from the viewer's perspective on each side of the vehicle.

I'm skipping the kit's default clockwork paint and instead building a custom paint job — cool highlights up top, darker shading below, and mud/grime buildup near the wheels for a weathered look.

Setting up the color palette with navy-gunmetal hull, hazard magenta, cyan, yellow, red, and blue accents, plus panel seam lines using fractional patterns along the hull surface. Now adding side skirts, mirrors, roof-mounted antennas with glowing red tips, vents, and a light bar.

Still placing lights and details... continuing with the roof strobe segments alternating red/blue glow, a cyan hood neon strip positioned just above the sloped hood surface, and rear tail light bars plus a "RIOT CONTROL" text plane facing backward on the rear doors.

I want the chevron texture's top oriented toward the front so it reads correctly, so I'll set up to [0,0,1] and place the decal plane around (0, 1.46, 2.05), then shift the hood's neon strip forward to z 2.45 to avoid overlapping. I'm also working out the hazard stripe texture, setting its axis direction and size so the pattern angles correctly across the surface.

Now I'm figuring out the wheel construction: each tire is a cylinder oriented along x, with a steel hub cylinder inside and a glowing cyan torus ring rotated to face outward as a neon accent, repeated across all six wheels with dark tread paint. For the cannon, I'm laying out a turret base as a lathe-shaped cylinder sitting on the roof, with a boxy turret body stacked above it, working out the exact y-position so it sits flush with the roof surface.

Writing barrel geometry...

Still placing hoses and tank geometry...

Still placing the plow geometry...

Positioning the chassis bottom, side skirt neon trim in magenta and cyan along both sides, and placing the windshield slope and side window dimensions relative to the roof geometry.

I realize the window box overshoots the actual body taper, so I'm recalculating the window outline as a trapezoid that follows the sloped roofline rather than a simple rectangle, checking body-top y-values at several z positions to fit the window shape properly underneath.

Making the glass a dark navy color, then adding small mirror boxes on rods at the sides, a roof light bar with alternating red/blue glow segments and a white center, and antenna rods with glowing red tips.

I'm also sketching rear details like taillights, a rear step, and dual spotlights, plus dark armored skirt panels along the body bottom and fender boxes. For branding, I'm planning a logo plate reading "KANG-TAO / PUBLIC ORDER" rendered with bold sans-serif text and stripe accents.

Now I'm defining helper functions for building boxes and glow effects, then writing the hull paint shader that blends dark base colors with lighter tones based on surface normals to create weathered, mud-streaked panels.

Setting up helper functions for boxes and glowing parts, and importing the stripes and glow utilities I'll need for the build.

Now I'm designing the texture SVGs: a dark blue windshield with cyan HUD lines and "ENFORCE" text, glowing hood chevrons, a logo panel with hazard borders, and a "RIOT CONTROL" rear label. I'm working out windshield placement and sizing to fit the 2.3-unit-wide body.

I'm checking plane orientations so the windshield and rear panel face the correct directions with upright text, confirming these parts are static with no bones or joints needed. Now I'm working out the hull extrusion outline, plotting the bottom edge points from rear to front.
